items.title: HLTH 2026: CVS Health, Cigna and Abridge collaborating with OpenAI to test computer-use agents
items.excerpt: OpenAI is expanding computer-use agents for healthcare that navigate EHR systems, payer portals and other software to handle repetitive manual tasks, with CVS Health, Cigna and Abridge testing them.

items.title: HLTH 2026: Suki unveils agentic OS to automate complex healthcare workflows
items.excerpt: Ambient clinical documentation company Suki launched Suki OS, an agentic operating system built on its ambient platform that links fragmented clinical software through unified AI agents, a partner ecosystem and a performance guarantee.

items.title: HLTH 2026: Viz.ai, Wolters Kluwer partner on platform integration
items.excerpt: Viz.ai will integrate Wolters Kluwer's UpToDate clinical evidence into its Viz.ai One AI disease-detection and care-coordination platform, which the companies call the first such integration into AI-driven care coordination workflows.

items.title: Apple, OpenEvidence launch conversational health AI study and app
items.excerpt: Apple launched a 200,000-participant Apple Health AI Usage Study with OpenEvidence to research what drives consumer trust in, and the quality of, conversational health AI answers; findings could inform Apple products.

items.title: Chest x-ray AI detects osteoporosis across seven countries
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: Promedius' PROS CXR: OSTEO, tested on 5,873 chest x-rays from 5,495 patients in seven countries, detected osteoporosis with pooled AUC 0.819, 87% sensitivity and 94% negative predictive value against DXA.

items.title: AI on chest x-rays matches PREVENT score for cardiac risk prediction
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: CNNs extracting coronary calcium and radiomics from chest x-rays of nearly 40,000 NLST and Mass General Brigham patients predicted MACE about as well as PREVENT (0.65 vs 0.66), and 0.71 combined.

items.title: Ultra-compact AI X-ray unit slashes ICU bedside imaging time
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: in a prospective 121-patient ICU study, Poskom's 1.3-kg AI-powered MiniAIR x-ray cut bedside imaging workflow time by more than 75% versus mobile DR while preserving diagnostic performance.

items.title: Opportunistic Risk Assessment of Major Osteoporotic Fractures from Routine Chest Radiographs Using Deep Learning
items.excerpt: Seoul National University Hospital radiologists report a deep-learning model that estimates major osteoporotic fracture risk from routine chest radiographs, enabling opportunistic screening without dedicated bone densitometry (date via Crossref created).

items.title: A Meta-Research Review of Statistical Practices for Image-Reliant AI Tools Predicting Lung Cancer Outcomes
items.excerpt: NEJM AI review audits the statistical methods behind published image-based AI tools that predict lung cancer outcomes, assessing how validation and reporting practices affect their clinical reliability (date via Crossref created).

items.title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery
items.excerpt: Nature Medicine presents OpenScientist, an open agentic AI co-scientist designed to analyze large, complex clinical and biomedical datasets and speed discovery that is otherwise limited by analyst time and domain expertise.

items.title: Dual chain-of-thought AI-PDCA framework for clinical history taking and documentation
items.excerpt: npj Digital Medicine study of an LLM-based AI-PDCA tutor that trains undergraduate medical students in clinical history taking and documentation with individualized, scalable feedback.

items.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model to predict the daily risk of febrile neutropenia in patients with AML undergoing chemotherapy
items.excerpt: Using registry data from two Finnish university hospital districts, researchers trained and validated an AI model predicting daily febrile neutropenia risk in acute myeloid leukemia patients during chemotherapy.

items.title: 계명대 동산병원, 다낭콩팥병 'AI 관리 플랫폼' 구축
items.excerpt: 계명대 동산병원이 유전성 신장질환인 다낭콩팥병 환자의 일상 건강관리를 돕는 인공지능(AI) 기반 통합관리 플랫폼을 구축했다.

items.title: Venture capitalist John Doerr says AI company, named for his late brother, could help fix primary care
items.excerpt: John Doerr backs Tom Health, a new AI tool for primary care named for his late brother, calling it 'one of the best possible uses of AI'.

items.title: Is AI Really Saving Hospitals Money? A New Study Raises Questions About the Cost of AI-Driven Care
items.excerpt: A New England Journal of Medicine study finds AI-generated care plans may cost far more than those ordered by physicians, challenging the savings case for clinical AI.

items.title: AI Model May Help Tailor Treatment for Childhood Brain Tumors
items.excerpt: Harvard/Dana-Farber's MANTIS model uses DNA methylation profiles from 2,786 children to predict 10-year survival in medulloblastoma and ependymoma, suggesting over half of average-risk medulloblastoma patients might get lower-dose radiation (Nature Genetics; needs prospective trials). (Off-list: no on-list coverage.)

items.title: Naitive Receives FDA 510(k) Clearance for OsteoSight Spine, Extending AI-Enabled Opportunistic Bone Health Assessment to Spine and Chest X-rays
items.excerpt: Naitive Technologies won FDA 510(k) clearance for OsteoSight Spine, extending its AI opportunistic bone-health assessment from routine x-rays to spine and chest films. (Off-list: no on-list coverage of this clearance.)

items.title: Cleerly's AI-powered plaque assessments outperform cardiac stress testing
items.excerpt: PARAMOUNT, a 530-patient randomized trial at 21 sites, found AI-based quantitative coronary CT plaque analysis (Cleerly) outperformed stress testing, cutting unnecessary cath-lab referrals for patients without obstructive CAD.

items.title: AI-derived inflammation score improves cardiovascular risk prediction beyond CAC
items.excerpt: A JAMA analysis from Oxford finds an AI-derived coronary inflammation score from noncontrast CT flags elevated cardiovascular risk even when calcium scores are zero, performing comparably to CCTA measures.

items.title: Beyond the Rogue Agent—Preparing Health Systems for AI Failure
items.excerpt: JAMA Viewpoint on how health systems should prepare for and stay resilient through failures of AI embedded in clinical operations (date via Crossref created, DOI 10.1001/jama.2026.24040).

items.title: KAIST's AI reads lips without sound, raising hopes for hearing assistance
items.excerpt: KAIST researchers built an AI lip-reading system that interprets clearer words first and uses context for ambiguous ones, which could eventually support communication for deaf and hard-of-hearing people.

items.title: Samsung, OpenAI push connected healthcare in US as Korea faces data barriers
items.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and OpenAI are expanding services connecting personal health data with U.S. hospitals for clinical use, while fragmented hospital IT and weak interoperability hold Korea back.

items.title: AI chatbots aren't therapists. But can they finally get men to open up?
items.excerpt: STAT examines whether AI chatbots, though imperfect therapists, can lower the barriers that keep men from seeking mental health care.

items.title: Insilico's AI-designed TEAD inhibitor shrank tumors in 4 of 22 mesothelioma patients; randomized Phase 2a planned for 2027
items.excerpt: Insilico Medicine's AI-designed pan-TEAD inhibitor ISM6331 produced responses in 4 of 22 pretreated mesothelioma patients; a randomized Phase 2a is planned for 2027. (Off-list: endpts/fiercebiotech had no coverage.)
